📖 Reading passage — Walt Disney (221 words) · tap to open

When people think of Walt Disney, they think of Mickey Mouse or Disneyland, but Walt Disney was a man who had to overcome difficulties to become successful.

From a young age, Walt loved to draw cartoons. He delivered newspapers every morning so that he could take art classes. He was known to fall asleep at school, but he continued to work hard.

When he was eighteen, he started a company with other artists. The company did not do well, so Walt decided to study animation. With his new skills, he started his second company. The company was successful at first, but then failed because of poor management.

However, Walt did not give up. He started a cartoon studio in Hollywood in 1923. This is where the idea of Mickey Mouse was born. As his studio grew, he started making animated films. His first film was Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.

Walt's creativity did not stop there. He wanted to create a park for children. In 1955, Disneyland was opened. Sixteen years later, Walt Disney World was opened.

In 1966, Walt discovered he had lung cancer. He died one month after doctors removed one of his lungs. Decades later, his legacy lives on through his famous quote: "All our dreams can come true, if we have the courage to pursue them."

        "Walt Disney is remembered for magic, but his story is really about courage. He delivered newspapers to afford art classes, and his early companies failed because of poor management. However, he did not give up. In 1923 he opened a cartoon studio in Hollywood, and Mickey Mouse was born. Later came Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, then Disneyland in 1955. In my opinion, his greatest legacy is not a castle but the idea that dreams can come true if we pursue them."
